Entropy is a leader in providing thermal technologies and simulation solutions for rugged embedded environments. We continue to produce and develop leading products that will achieve, and help test, maximum operating performance for electronic systems in harsh environments.
With the current focus on interoperability, and the relentless increase of thermal power density in silicon devices, embedded systems and ruggedized chassis need a focus on driving SWAP-C optimisation more than ever. Our solutions, with new technology and excellent engineering, target the mechanical packaging opportunities this challenge provides and allows our customers to produce best in class products.
Using extensive experience working in MilAero packaging design, we also support: design of improved thermal solutions for all VITA-48.x and IEEE1101.x specifications, provide predictive life simulations to support VITA-51.x, and validate extended shock and vibration requirements in accordance with MIL-STD-810 and GEVS-SE.
Entropy specialises exclusively in the Defence, Avionics and Space giving our customers improved design confidence and reduced time to delivery that other solutions providers can not. We focus primarily on the root cause of thermal loading, which is typically the silicon core architecture of the product and have optimised the methods extracting heat from these devices. In order to be highly effective, our approach uses detailed chip level modelling of devices such as:
• Intel Core, Xeon and Atom processors
• Xilinx Ultrascale+
• Nvidia Jetson SoM, Quadro Turing, Pascal and GTX
• AMD Ryzen and Epyc
All our solutions are carefully validated against representative testing data. We are confident that by using first class experience in this challenging industry, by rigorously employing engineering fundamental principles, and the application of leading simulation skills that your product will be as ready for the field as possible.

Founded in 1968 and independently managed since January 1st 2012, the University of Toulon (UTLN) places the University’s attractiveness at the core of its long-term strategic plan.
Well-established throughout the region, the University of Toulon works closely with the region’s social and economic institutions to tailor its academic programmes and research activities to their needs.
The University of Toulon is an interdisciplinary institution with 3 campuses. The University offers a hundred different degrees (excluding medical school) and operates 15 Research Units.

Some research activities at the university of Toulon involve spatial Earth Observation. In particular, the Mediterranean Institute of Oceanography makes use of satellite data to complement the biophysical observation and modeling of the ocean surface. It is also operating oceanographic HF radars for the real-time monitoring of coastal Mediterranean surface currents. These measurements can be very valuable for the calibration & validation of coastal altimetric missions or Doppler-based surface currents measurements.

The "Laboratoire Informatique et Systèmes" (LIS) is an engineering science laboratory, bringing together computer scientists and signal processing and control process researchers. LIS researchers are working in the field of deep learning, signal and image processing, optimal control.

Professor Rolf Rossaint, a co-founder of Docs in Clouds, got the initial idea in 2004: Could telemedicine/telehealth be used to optimize processes for German emergency services, ensure quality of service, and improve the deployment of medical personnel? After 10 years of R+D, the Emergency TeleDoc system was conceived, and it hasbeen an integral part of the local emergency services of Aachen since 2014. With the help of our partner company,P3 telehealthcare, all ambulances were retrofitted with the TeleDoc system, and we established a communication hub staffed 24/7. Inspired by this success, other local communities are currently adopting the system. More information atwww.telenotarzt.de.

Since then, we expanded our focus on other fields, which benefit from telemedical applications. Our TeleDoc software now support general practioners, nursing homes and outpatient nursing services. Currently, our company is organized into three business units: Telecare (focuses on telemedicine for nursing and medical care), Medical Engineering Services and Innovation (Research & Development). Because biomedical engineering is a multidisciplinary field, our team includes both physicians and engineers, which work hand in hand. This interaction allows us to develop products and provide services that fit the current market need. Our physicians contribute with medical input; in addition, they are aware of the current clinical weaknesses and needs. Our engineers, in turn, develop solutions combining technical knowledge, innovation, creativity and practicality. What drives us: Bringing medical care to people, faster and more effectively!
Despite of the medical background, our products do not necessarily need to be applied in the medical field. In fact, they can be translated to other areas. This is the case of the TeleExpert system: specialists can offer prompt support anywhere in the world. Within this context, project costs, operational costs, and more importantly, time can be saved.

With a history that dates back to 1969, INDAERO consolidates as a company in 2002 by manufacturing engraved plates and labels for AIRBUS. Two years later, it makes its way into the world of machining, expanding its services in the manufacture of aeronautical parts, and subsequently certifying itself to the EN9100 Aerospace standard.
In 2010, it expanded its area radius and began to export products in Europe, specifically to Austria and Poland. Two years later, it forms the GRUPO EMERGY business alliance in which, thanks to its strategic union with UNS, it achieves an immersion in the sheet metal transformation market, including laser cutting, folding and manual and robotic welding processes.
Since 2013, GRUPO EMERGY began to work with additive manufacturing, using high resistance thermoplastics to manufacture hybrid tools and soluble molds for composites. In 2017 it achieved international recognition thanks to its participation in the AIRBUS NH90 project.
In 2018, thanks to a wide investment in technology, among which 5-axis CNC's and a 6-axis Absolute Arm measuring arm stand out, GRUPO EMERGY manages to enter the Aerospace sector with high-precision machining for very important international projects.
Thanks to the avant-garde vision of its work team, its resilience and constant investment in technology, GRUPO EMERGY has today more than 1,750 square meters of facilities, which provide its customers with a comprehensive service and cutting-edge technology, at your fingertips.

CoopCulture is one of the leading players in the field of cultural heritage in Italy and its core business is strictly linked to the promotion and the access of cultural heritage through specialized services’ systems and new storytellings.
CoopCulture works in almost every region of the country, managing 250 cultural sites including some of Italian main landmarks -such as the Colosseum in Rome, the National Archeological Museum in Naples, the Blue Cave at Capri isle, the Temples’ Valley in Agrigento- and many less known cultural sites and areas, historically and artistically very rich.
CoopCulture offers work position to more than 1700 employees who welcome more than 13,5 millions visitors per year, that benefit of multiple cultural products designed and implemented by our Research & Development division.
CoopCulture offers a wide range of products and services aimed to empower tourists’ cultural experiences:
· at museums and exhibitions, CoopCulture manages welcoming services, booking and ticketing offices, didactics, marketing & communication services, bookshop and culture concept stores;
· at libraries and archives, CoopCulture manages activities such as: library management, computerized cataloguing, public services for reading and borrowing, educational services and workshop activities;
· in order to give value to the so called overspread heritage and to all linked territories, CoopCulture is able to promote complex networking systems through integrated touristic cards and territorial digital platforms.
CoopCulture deeply works on audience development, aiming to enlarge audiences in terms of numbers, to wide the range of different cultural audiences (attracting the youth and the elderly, working for people with special needs, involving also people coming from different cultural and social backgrounds), and to increase the relationship with them.
The concept of deepening relations, diversifying audiences, engaging the so- called new users has recently been stressed through the powerful raid of the new technological paradigm and the digital revolution which have fully and deeply modified the access and the distribution of cultural products despite of social and economical barriers.
That is why, from the ‘90s till up today, all around Italy CoopCulture’s audiences have been able to count on several technological tools: from the audio and video guides, which started supporting guide tours at the end of the last century, to the first MP3’s for kids and the first audioguide based on the Italian language of signs. Later on, our researches for new ways of engaging people have brought us, first, in 2015, to the experience of the Critic Globus, a big egg placed at the second stair of the Colosseum, which visitors entered in order to record own evaluations about the Earth as “mother of life”, as main topic of a linked temporary exhibitions; then, in the same year, to analyze users’ needs while travelling within territories in order to design the ArtPlanner, a digital platform dedicated to local areas and overspread heritage and to those temporary citizens who want to explore and experience different cultural life styles by customizing their own itineraries; to Caracalla IV Dimension in 2017, a headset housing a mobile phone and dedicated software, which allows visitors to explore in virtual reality, the ancient Baths of Caracalla in Rome as they really looked like in 216 AD.
